transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess mostly I’ve been feeling… tired, more than I think I should be. I mean, I can sleep, and I’m still keeping up with work okay, so it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything. But even before the day really gets going, I feel like I’m already running on a low battery. I wasn’t sure if that was enough of a reason to come in, but it’s been bothering me.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you normally like to do?

I still do them, mostly. I mean, I go fishing sometimes, I tend my tomatoes, I’ll go to a church concert if there’s one on… so it’s not like I’ve stopped everything. But if I’m being honest, for a long time now it’s felt kind of gray and flat most days. Things I used to look forward to feel more like something I’m checking off a list than something I’m really enjoying. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way, with things seeming gray and flat?

It’s been… a while. I’d say it really started around when I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work. That was about two years and four months ago, I think. I kept telling myself it was just the responsibility and that I was handling it fine, but the gray feeling has kind of stuck around since then.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

A few, I guess… I still go fishing sometimes, and I mess around with the tomatoes in the garden, and I’ll go to a church concert now and then. So I don’t want to make it sound like I get no enjoyment at all.

But… for a long time now, most days it’s had this gray, flat feeling to it. Even the things I used to really look forward to can feel more like I’m just checking them off a list than actually enjoying them. If that makes sense.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasurable?

Yeah… I suppose so. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still do some of them. But fishing, working with the tomatoes, going to a church concert—those used to be things I’d really look forward to.

Now a lot of the time they just feel kind of… gray, I guess. Like I’m doing them because they’re good things to do, or because I should, more than because I’m really getting pleasure out of them. More like checking something off a list, if that makes sense.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Some, yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like there’s nothing. I can still get something out of fishing, or tending the tomatoes, or a church concert once in a while.

But if I’m being honest, most days it’s still pretty gray and flat. Those things used to feel like something I looked forward to, and now a lot of the time they feel more like… items on a checklist. Like I’m doing them because they’re good things to do, not because I’m really enjoying them the way I used to. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in and look forward to, without feeling like you're just going through the motions?

Not really in the way I used to, no. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m miserable every second or anything… but for a long time now most days have had that gray, flat feeling.

Fishing, the tomatoes, a church concert—those are probably the closest things. And sometimes I’m glad I did them. But looking forward to them and really enjoying them without that “going through the motions” feeling… that’s been pretty rare. A lot of the time it’s more like I’m just doing the right things, checking them off, if that makes sense.
Are there any days where you feel like you're able to enjoy things without that gray, flat feeling?

There are probably a few moments here and there, yes… I don’t want to say it’s every single day or that nothing ever feels good.

But whole days where that gray, flat feeling isn’t there? Not many, if I’m being honest. For a long time now, most days it’s kind of in the background. Even things I used to really look forward to—fishing, working with the tomatoes, going to a church concert—can still feel more like I’m checking them off a list than really enjoying them.

I hope that makes sense.
Have you felt this gray, flat feeling for more than two years now?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been about two years and four months now, since I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work.

That’s when I really started noticing that gray, flat feeling settling in most days. Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Have you experienced this gray, flat feeling almost every day since it started?

Almost every day… yes, I’d say most days. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I can still do things and there are little moments that aren’t terrible.

But that gray, flat feeling has been there a lot—kind of in the background. Even with things I used to enjoy, like fishing or tending the tomatoes or going to a church concert, it often feels more like something I’m checking off than something I’m really taking pleasure in.

Is that the kind of “almost every day” you mean?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes… I think I have, though I don’t want to make it sound like I never enjoy anything at all.

It’s more that for a long time now, there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days. Things I used to look forward to—like fishing, tending the tomatoes, even going to a church concert—sometimes feel more like items on a checklist than something I’m really enjoying.

I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but that’s how it feels.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

A little, I guess… I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything.

My appetite’s just been off more days than not. I’ll get busy and work through lunch without really noticing, and then at dinner I kind of pick at it. My wife’s mentioned my pants are fitting looser, so… I suppose there has been some weight change. Does that count as significant?
Have you had thoughts about death or dying recently?

No… not really. I mean, I know I’m getting older, so the subject crosses your mind now and then in a normal way, I suppose.

But I haven’t been sitting around thinking about death or wanting to die, if that’s what you mean. At least, I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy and still enjoy without feeling like you're just going through the motions?

I’m trying to think of one… I mean, there are moments, sure. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is awful all the time.

But if I’m being honest, even the things I’d normally say I enjoy—fishing, working with the tomatoes, going to a church concert—most of the time they’ve got that same sort of gray, flat feeling around them. Like I’m doing them because they’re things I do, not because I’m really looking forward to them.

Maybe every now and then I get a little spark of it, but it doesn’t seem to last. Is that answering what you mean?
Have you felt this gray, flat feeling for most of the past two years or more?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, but it really started when I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work, and that was about two years and four months ago.

Since then, that gray feeling has been there more often than not. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in and look forward to without feeling like you're just doing them out of habit?

I wish I could say yes. I mean, I do still do some of those things—fishing, fussing with the tomatoes, going to a church concert if there is one—and I’m not miserable every second of it or anything.

But most days it’s more like… I’m checking off something I’m supposed to enjoy. There’s this gray, flat feeling over it, and I don’t really look forward to it the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Some, maybe, but not the way I used to. I don’t want to make it sound like I never enjoy anything, but for a long time now there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days.

Even things I’d usually look forward to—fishing, working on the tomatoes, maybe a church concert—often feel more like items on a checklist than something I’m really taking pleasure in. I hope that makes sense.
Has this gray, flat feeling you've described lasted for two years or more without any significant breaks?

Yes… I’d say so. I mean, there might be better days here and there, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I haven’t had what I’d call a real break from it.

It’s been going on since I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work, and that was about two years and four months ago. Does that answer it the way you mean?
Has this gray, flat feeling you've described been present for the majority of the time since it started, without any periods of at least two months where you felt completely back to normal?

Yes, I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, because I’ve had better stretches here and there, but I wouldn’t say I ever felt completely back to normal for a couple months or anything like that.

It’s basically been there since I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work, about two years and four months ago. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Has this gray, flat feeling you've described been present for the majority of the time since it started?

Yes, most of the time, I’d say. Not every single minute, and I do have days that are a little lighter, but for a long while now that gray, flat feeling is there more often than not.

Even things like fishing or working on my tomatoes, or going to a church concert… I’ll still do them, but a lot of the time they feel more like something I’m supposed to get through than something I’m really enjoying. Is that what you’re asking?
